# HFilterBar

> Wrapping filters with an application-owned clear request.

[Start with the Hearth UI agent index](../../../llms.txt). This describes repository source for version 0.7.0. Match documentation to your installed source/release.

## Identity

- Vue export: `HFilterBar` from `@hearth-ui/vue`.
- Custom element: `<hearth-filter-bar>`.
- Constructor: `HearthFilterBarElement` from `@hearth-ui/elements`.
- Category: Controls.
- [Implementation](https://github.com/samishal1998/hearth-ui/blob/main/src/components/HFilterBar.vue).

## Choose and use it correctly

- clear requests resetting all application filters; the component does not discover or mutate child models. Compose chip groups, switches, inputs, and buttons in the default slot.

## Public API

label, activeCount, disabled

A `?` marks optional source props. Props with defaults may be omitted. Internal `formDisabled` and `control-sync` plumbing is excluded below; do not use it in application code.

```ts
type Props = {
    label?: string;
    activeCount?: number;
    disabled?: boolean;
};
```

### Defaults

```ts
{ label: "Filters", activeCount: 0 }
```

### Events

clear()

```ts
type Emits = {
    clear: [
    ];
};
```

Vue-emitted custom-element events expose argument arrays in `event.detail`. Listen on the element. Native events such as `click` retain their normal payloads. The elements package provides framework-independent DOM event types.

### Slots

default

Vue uses `<template #slotName>`; custom elements use `<div slot="slotName">`. Web components do not support Vue scoped slots.

### CSS parts

base

Use `hearth-filter-bar::part(part-name)` for an exposed part or inherited `--h-*` tokens for shared styling. Native Vue components use the shared stylesheet and `h-*` classes.

## Vue example

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { HFilterBar, HInput } from '@hearth-ui/vue';
import '@hearth-ui/vue/styles.css';
function clear() { /* Reset application-owned filter models. */ }
</script>

<template>
  <HFilterBar :active-count="2" @clear="clear"><HInput label="Search" hide-label type="search" /></HFilterBar>
</template>
```

## Web-component example

Provide a mount point. For field submission, use an owning native form; the auth page already contains its own form.

```html
<div id="example"></div>
```

This is bundler-based ESM. For raw HTML, load `dist/themes.css` with a link and import `registerElements` from `./dist/elements/index.js` instead. Initial array/object properties are assigned before connection to establish reset defaults.

```js
import { registerElements } from '@hearth-ui/elements';
import '@hearth-ui/elements/themes.css';
registerElements();

const mount = document.querySelector('#example');
const element = document.createElement('hearth-filter-bar');
Object.assign(element, {
  "activeCount": 2
});

element.innerHTML = "<hearth-input label=\"Search\" hide-label type=\"search\"></hearth-input>"; // Static example markup only; never inject untrusted HTML.

element.addEventListener('clear', event => {
  const [value] = event.detail;
  // Update your application state using value.
});

mount.append(element);
```
